questions.q: Which river, Italy's longest, rises in the Alps of western Piedmont and flows east past Turin across the whole of northern Italy?
questions.exp: The Po rises on Monte Viso near the French border, gathers the Tanaro and the other rivers of Piedmont, and runs east across the broad Po Valley to its delta south of Venice. The Court names it as Piedmont's body of water, with the Alps and the Apennines, which wall the region on three sides, as its mountains.

questions.q: The eastern Barolo communes of Serralunga d'Alba, Monforte d'Alba and Castiglione Falletto stand on older, sandier ground that gives denser, longer lived wine. Which geological formation is it?
questions.exp: The Court's soil cell asks for the difference within Barolo: Serravallian sandstone and compacted marl (once called Helvetian) in the east gives firm, slow wines, while the younger, bluish Tortonian marl of La Morra and Barolo gives perfume and earlier charm. Kimmeridgian and Portlandian are the clays and limestones of Chablis.

questions.q: Of Barbaresco's minimum ageing before release, how many months must be spent in wood?
questions.exp: Barbaresco must age at least 26 months, counted from 1 November of the harvest year, with nine of them in wood, against Barolo's 38 months with 18 in wood; a Barbaresco Riserva needs 50 months in all.

questions.q: In the trade, what word names the standard bottling of Barolo or Barbaresco, released after the basic minimum ageing rather than held back for the Riserva?
questions.exp: Normale, one of the Court's two label terms here, is the everyday name for the standard Barolo or Barbaresco against the Riserva, which ages 62 months for Barolo and 50 for Barbaresco. Neither denomination has a Superiore or a Classico tier, and Vigna introduces a named vineyard.

questions.q: Autumn fog drifts off the Alpine foothills and settles in the Langhe valleys at harvest time. What is the local word for it?
questions.exp: Nebbia is the Court's general term for the fog that fills the Langhe valleys in autumn, and Nebbiolo is usually said to take its name from it, either from the fog of its late harvest or from the misty bloom on its berries.

questions.q: Piedmont's most planted red grape, high in acid and low in tannin, is bottled under several denominations. Which of these carries DOCG rank?
questions.exp: Barbera d'Asti is the DOCG the Court names for dry red Barbera, at least 90 per cent of the grape from the Asti and Monferrato hills, with Nizza carved out of it as a DOCG of its own in 2014; Barbera d'Alba, Piemonte and Colli Tortonesi are DOCs.

questions.q: Which of these named vineyards lies in the Barbaresco zone rather than in Barolo?
questions.exp: Asili stands with Ovello, Montestefano and Pora among the Court's top Barbaresco vineyards; Cannubi, Brunate and Monprivato are the three top Barolo sites it names, each now an official vineyard name a label may carry.

questions.q: Which ageing vessel became the badge of the modernist Barolo and Barbaresco producers in the 1980s and 1990s?
questions.exp: The modernists paired short, warm macerations and rotary fermenters with small new French barriques for colour, softness and earlier appeal; the traditionalists kept long macerations and large old Slavonian botti, and most houses now sit somewhere between the two camps.
